# Costs

Actual spend: **$0**. Everything ran on free tiers: Gemini API free tier, Cloudflare Workers AI's 10,000
neurons/day, Kaggle's ~30 GPU-hours/week, and a local Mac. The table below is **measured** from `runs.jsonl` by
`make costs`. The USD column is a **list-price equivalent**: what the same calls would cost on paid tiers,
using the prices in `config.toml [prices]` (sources and date there). GPU minutes include model download
and load time (`_load` lines), because that is what the Kaggle quota counts.

### Music: GPU time correction

The table counts 86.4 s (1.4 GPU min) for music, but the first ACE-Step run (one take, 2026-11-25) ran for
**231 s (3.9 min)** on the Kaggle T4. Its kernel log, `outputs/logs/heritage-acestep_af58197c.log` (each
line's `time` is seconds since the kernel started), splits that time like this:

| Part | Time | In `runs.jsonl`? |
|---|---|---|
| Set-up: clone ACE-Step, install 141 packages (1 min 37 s), start the server, load the model | 140 s | no |
| Generating the take | 86.4 s | yes |
| Kaggle saving the run's output | 5 s | no |
| **Kernel total** | **231 s** | |

The worker logged only the generation, so the stage's real total is the kernel time, 231 s. That total already
contains the 86.4 s of generation, so nothing is added on top of it. Since this fix (2026-11-25) the worker
also logs its set-up as a `_load` line, as the Wan worker does. The six-take run was pushed before the fix,
so its set-up time also has to be read from its kernel log.

The "about 23 minutes" noted earlier was the time from pushing the job (07:41 EAT) to seeing `COMPLETE` in
`make kaggle-status`. The take's line in `runs.jsonl` is stamped 07:45 EAT, so most of those minutes came
after the job had finished, not while it ran.
